title: Many rooms (John 14:1–7)
hookLine: let not your heart be troubled; in my Father's house are many rooms
carry: let not your heart be troubled

cards: Some houses keep a room ready: the bed made up, a towel on the end of it. Someone thought of the guest before the guest arrived. Now go back to that supper table.
Judas has gone. Jesus has just told Peter he'll deny him. He's said he's leaving, and they can't come yet.
The room is full of fear; their whole lives have been built around following this man for years. And the first thing he says to them is about their hearts.

teach.b: "Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me." A few days ago Jesus himself said, now is my soul troubled. He knows the feeling from inside.

He isn't scolding them for being afraid; he's giving them somewhere to put the fear. Then: "In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you."
Mansions sounds like big estates on a hill.

But in the English of the King James Bible, a mansion simply meant a dwelling place. The Greek word is monē, from a verb meaning to remain, to abide, and that verb will be all over the next chapter: abide in me.
So the picture isn't a gated community. It's a big family house with room for everyone, a place to stay and not have to leave. Many rooms: no shortage, no waiting list.
And Jesus goes ahead to get them ready, like someone making up the bed before a guest arrives.

teach.h: THOMAS: HOW CAN WE KNOW THE WAY?
teach.b: Thomas says it plainly: "Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?" And Jesus answers: "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me."

teach.h: LET NOT YOUR HEART BE TROUBLED.
teach.b: Christians hold this line at the center of their faith in Jesus. Churches have long talked about what it means for people of other paths, and they don't all answer it the same way.
For Thomas, at that table, it meant: you don't need a map. You need me.

how: Christians often read these words at funerals and memorial services, and some also pray "let not your heart be troubled" in times of worry.

o: nod along and hope to figure it out later.
"Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?"

practice: If you can, tidy a corner, a couch, a chair where someone could sit; if not, picture a room in your home and imagine who might come, a friend, a relative, a stranger who needs somewhere to stay.
Picture making it ready with care: clean sheets, a glass of water, a light left on. If you pray, give thanks for a place made ready for you; if not, enjoy the thought of welcoming someone.

wordCard.voice: Many rooms. Jesus's promise at the supper: in my Father's house are many dwelling places, and he goes ahead to prepare one.

orig.note: Greek: a dwelling, a place to stay. From menō, to remain or abide.
